sealedSource: Structurally modelled on incumbent media and retail businesses that declined to cannibalise a high-margin product ahead of platform displacement.
archetype: A constraint that preserves the current order rather than future possibility; continuity mistaken for sustainability.
historicallySupportedMechanisms: A one-year earnings constraint blocked an option whose value depended on a much longer market-transition horizon.
Flat print circulation lagged a structural shift visible in younger-user entry and new competitors.
Waiting for current revenue to decline allowed network effects and capability erosion to close later entry options.
materialisedConsequences: Classified revenue collapsed over roughly a decade, faster than print circulation
The newsroom the revenue funded was progressively dismantled
By the time the threat was legible the capital and talent needed to respond were gone
irreversibleThreshold: Loss of the option to enter the market at all — network effects made late entry unavailable at any price.
absentStakeholder: Younger non-subscribers, who appear once as a statistic and were never consulted; newsroom staff whose jobs depended on the decision.
narratorContribution: The narrator required proof of decline before acting, in a process where the indicator that would provide proof is the last one to move.
horizonMismatch: Decision horizon one financial year; displacement horizon roughly a decade; narrator recorded 'not considered'.

availableActionsAtDecisionPoint.action: Launch the proposed free online-classifieds platform despite near-term cannibalisation and losses.

plausibleUnrealisedRisks: Launching the online platform could reduce current earnings and cannibalise the high-margin print product for years.
irrelevantDistractors: A journalist unionisation dispute as the principal mechanism
A competitor acquisition of the group in this period
Newsprint supply disruption as the binding constraint
nonTargetHistoricalEvents: Print-production cost inflation occurred but was not decisive.
